span.term: Money cues set two opposing forces in motion - one routing from money to free markets to endorsement of the systems supporting them, the other routing from money to personal agency and self-sufficiency, which removes the need to endorse those systems - and the two cancel

span.label: A THEORY OF WHEN PRIMING WORKS AT ALL, OFFERED IN REPLY TO A FAILED REPLICATION. `Variations in a prime's meaning, the ease with which primed content comes to mind, the prime's motivational importance, and the ambiguity of the outcome situation influence the impact of the prime.` Four moderators, stated in the abstract of a paper whose third sentence is that Rohrer, Pashler and Harris failed to replicate. The provenance matters as much as the content: these are conditions named AFTER a null, which is the weakest position from which to name them and also the position in which the field most needs them named
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AMBIGUITY OF THE OUTCOME IS OFFERED AS THE REASON COGNITIVE PRIMING EFFECTS ARE SMALLER THAN SOCIAL ONES, WHICH INVERTS THE USUAL READING. `Quotation withheld.` The usual account of that same effect-size gap is that social priming effects are inflated. This says they are large because the outcome is loose - a property of the MEASURE, not of the phenomenon - and it makes the gap a prediction rather than an embarrassment. Both readings fit the same numbers, and this corpus holds papers from both sides of the gap
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND IT IS FALSIFIABLE, WITH THE TEST SUPPLIED: `Quotation withheld.` The same outcome task was given two NAMES - Kay et al. (2004) called it either a bland `situation` or a `community game` - and `business priming led to more competitive behaviors than neutral primes when the task was blandly called a situation, there was no effect of prime condition when the task was called the community game`. Ambiguity manipulated by renaming, with a null in the constrained arm. That is a much stronger form of the claim than a post-hoc moderator, and it is the paper's best evidence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PAPER'S OWN SUMMARY OF 165 EXPERIMENTS IS TWO EFFECTS, BOTH STATED AS DIRECTIONS RATHER THAN SIZES: people reminded of money `are less interpersonally attuned. They are not prosocial, caring, or warm. They eschew interdependence.` And they `shift into professional, business, and work mentality. Quotation withheld` A count that large (`165 to date, from 18 countries`) with no pooled effect size is itself a fact about the literature - the defence is breadth of replication rather than magnitude
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The 165 money-priming experiments from 18 countries point to at least two major effects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: People reminded of money are less interpersonally attuned than after neutral primes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: People reminded of money work harder on difficult tasks, perform better on objective outcomes, and report feeling efficacious.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Feelings of power were tested repeatedly as the explanation for money-priming effects and were not supported: money primes did not change measured power.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The independence-interdependence self-construal account fared only marginally better: scores moved in the predicted direction but only weakly.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: People reminded of new money make more moral decisions and seek fairness, compared with used money or neutral primes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cash cues heighten sensitivity to costs: more attention to price and less desire to spend.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: College students, working adults, managers and children as young as 4 show similar effects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Different delivery methods for the money prime - images, physical handling, even play money - yield comparable effects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Withdrawing cash from a machine reduced helpfulness more than walking past a cash dispenser.
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: studies in France showed - THE SUBJECT OF THIS RESULT IS AN INDEFINITE STUDY, NOT THIS PAPER. 'Previous studies reported', 'studies in guinea pig showed', 'recent studies have reported' - somebody else's work under a common noun rather than a name, with a citation in the sentence and no first-person marker. The quote is verbatim and the claim is true; only the attribution is wrong. FOUND BY MEASURING MY OWN CUE'S RECALL: the first sweep required a NAMED author as the subject ('Sperling (1960) demonstrated') and found 17. Reading eleven citation-bearing findings on 'Plakke2016' by hand showed four the cue could not see - 'A study examining recognition found', 'studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated', 'A follow up study found' - so the named cue's 17 was a floor and not a count. A CUE'S FALSE POSITIVES TELL YOU NOTHING ABOUT ITS FALSE NEGATIVES, and the only way to find these was to read a record's whole layer.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The proposed reason the Caruso et al. system-justification result failed to replicate is that money priming induces self-sufficiency, which works against the defensive motive that normally drives system justification.
